While I was a sophomore at the University of Iowa, I was a part of the Basic Drawing class. This class was just like any other drawing class but one of my assignments was to finish a pen. My professor bought all 23 of us new pens and told us to draw until the pen became empty. I was baffled that she thought we could finish an entire pen in a week because I hadn’t even finished a pen since last year.

I couldn’t figure out what to draw in the first place. I was searching for still life that I could come back to after a few hours and it would still be the same. That eliminated all options for public spaces and since it was winter I crossed off the idea of going outdoors. While in my friend’s dorm room, I decided that their closet should be my muse. I was already in there about 3 times a day so staying a little longer didn’t faze me. So, by asking for permission and them accepting, I took that pen in hand, and drew.

I spent about 27 hours working on this piece to show the world what the inside of a dorm room closet looked like. The only thing I wish I could change is where I stopped drawing. After showing my professor, she asked me what the rest of the room looked like and asked why I didn’t continue. I explained, “Well, on the other half of the room they had a mini fridge and some packages thrown around. There was food lying around and they kept some more of their shoes over there. It was too messy to draw.” She told me that she wished I had continued, telling me that it would only add to the art and make it that much more unique. By erasing out the mess in their room, I didn’t capture the true essence that their room gave off. I think I failed them in a way but at least I can show the world their closet.
